newsitem.title: USA: Genzyme denied FDA panel nod on Sepracoat.
newsitem.headline: Genzyme denied FDA panel nod on Sepracoat.

text.p: Genzyme Corp said on Monday that a U.S. Food and Drug Administration panel voted 6 to 0 against granting the company approval for its Sepracoat coating solution to reduce adhesions in abdominal and pelvic surgery.
Genzyme said the general and plastic surgery devices panel said the product appeared to be safe, but said the company had not presented sufficient evidence of its clinical effectiveness.
The panel's recommendation, while not binding, usually is followed by the FDA, the company said.
In August the FDA had approved Genzyme's Seprafilm product for reducing adhersions from direct surgical trauma. Sepracoat is intended to treat indirect trauma, such as incidental abrasions.

"We are disappointed, but this result was not entirely unexpected, because this was a very tough clinical model," said Henri Termeer, Genzyme's chairman, in a statement. "This will not affect Seprafilm. We will consider options for further clinical studies of Sepracoat, possibly in combination with Seprafilm."
Genzyme is a biotechnology and health-care products company. Its shares closed down 2-7/16 to 22-5/16 on Monday.
